alignments.note: A construct noun cannot carry the article, so the English 'the' before 'porch' is supplied by the chain's definiteness and stays with this noun (rule 29).
The 'of' of the construct chain belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19).

Hebrew has no relative adverb: 'asher ... sham' is the locative relative construction, and the ASV spends one English word, 'where', on it, so the whole expression is one unit headed on the morpheme carrying the locative lexeme (rule 30, whose 'wherein' is the same relative-plus-resumptive idiom, and rule 35's 'kol asher' -> 'whatsoever'). The intervening verb keeps its own unit. Reading 'sham' as a resumptive element left unrepresented under rule 22 remains defensible, but rule 22 governs a repetition of the same element, not the parts of an idiom.
The inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun and the periphrastic 'was to' with the lexical verb as head (rule 17).

'even' is the appositional marker the ASV supplies for the asyndetic resumption of the noun, and 'the' is supplied for the construct noun; both belong to this unit rather than being 'added'. Reading 'even' as 'added' remains defensible.
The ASV writes 'of judgment' without an article; the single English 'the' in the phrase is the one supplied for the construct 'porch'.
Construct chain 'of' heads on the nomen rectum (rule 19).
The ASV fronts the verb; reordered target tokens may form one unit (rule 25).
The passive participle supplies its own subject and copula in English; the lexical participle is the head (rule 24).
The article assimilated into the pointed preposition is a real token, but the ASV writes 'with cedar' without 'the' (rule 12).
The ASV writes 'from floor to floor' without articles.
The ASV writes 'to floor' without an article.
